name: Build Peak Release Duration Arc
use_when: A scene builds toward a climax, reveal, success, failure, or emotional impact.
The edit needs momentum without losing the consequence after the peak.
A montage or sequence feels like it ends too abruptly after the strongest beat.
A short-form section needs a sound/cut intensity build followed by a clear drop or open-space reset.
avoid_when: The sequence is purely informational and does not need an emotional peak.
The story point is meant to feel sudden, clipped, or unresolved.
The source material lacks enough reaction or aftermath footage.

timeline_pattern.build: Shot durations gradually compress toward the peak.
timeline_pattern.peak: The strongest action or emotional beat gets clear emphasis.
timeline_pattern.release: After the peak, shots lengthen so the viewer can feel consequence.
timeline_pattern.ratio: Release can be equal to or longer than the build when the emotion is failure, loss, awe, or disappointment.
timeline_pattern.contrast_drop_rule: For short-form contrast drops, the release can be a very brief black/open-space reset when it follows a real build and re-enters cleanly.

motion.rule: Motion intensity may rise during the build and settle during release.
motion.avoid: Continuing high-energy motion after a beat that needs emotional aftermath.

sound.rule: Build sound energy toward the peak, then leave space or soften the mix for release.
sound.contrast_stack: Risers, whooshes, denser cuts, ambience, or impacts can build contrast before the drop; the next line must remain intelligible.
sound.avoid: Cutting music/effects so abruptly that the emotional aftermath disappears.

captions.rule: Keep captions efficient during the build and sparse during the release if faces carry the feeling.

color.rule: Keep grade consistent through the arc; do not let peak effects make release shots feel unrelated.

implementation.ffmpeg: Assemble segment durations in a JSON or EDL and inspect the duration curve. Render a short sequence to test whether the release has enough time.
implementation.remotion: Store shot durations as an array and verify the build compresses and the release expands after the peak.
implementation.blender: Use animation intensity curves that rise to the peak and ease down during release.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Manually shorten clips into the climax, then extend reaction/aftermath clips after it.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use markers for setup, peak, and release. Compare sequence versions with different post-peak durations.

common_mistakes: Dropping to silence or black without enough buildup for the release to read as intentional.
Compressing the emotional consequence more than the buildup.
Making every shot shorter without shaping a release.
Letting effects continue at peak intensity after the story needs aftermath.
qc: Is there a clear build, peak, and release?
Does the post-peak section give enough time to feel consequence?
Do shot durations support the emotion rather than only the beat?
Does the sequence still work without explaining the intended arc?
If using a contrast drop, does it follow a visible/audible build and re-enter cleanly?
